description: This pie chart, titled “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” visually represents the distribution of media outlets categorized by their framing influence, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet or group and its associated numerical value. The chart is divided into 15 distinct segments, each labeled with the name of a media entity and a number indicating its relative weight or score. The largest segment is “Breitbart,” colored blue and labeled with the value 14, followed by “Drudge Report” (orange, value 8) and “The Daily Caller” (green, value 8). Other notable segments include “NPR” (red, value 7) and “The Huffington Post” (purple, value 7). Smaller segments include “Vox” (brown, 6), “The Guardian” (pink, 5), and “BBC” (gray, 4). The chart also includes several outlets with a value of 3: “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” “CNN,” “PoliticusUSA,” and “Shareblue,” each represented by a different color. A large gray segment labeled “Other” accounts for the remaining portion of the chart. The chart includes a legend, though it is not fully visible in the image, and each slice is labeled with its corresponding value, with no slices appearing to be exploded or visually emphasized beyond their size. The segments are arranged in a clockwise order, generally descending in size from the largest to the smallest, with the exception of “Other,” which is placed at the bottom right.
